study type: Secondary analysis of a multi-center randomized controlled trial
exposure: Chlorhexidine-alcohol and iodine combined sequentially skin preparation
cohort: The study participants were 2013 women who were at least 24 weeks gestation and undergoing unscheduled cesarean delivery, originally part of a trial comparing adjunctive azithromycin versus placebo.
finding: The type of skin preparation used (iodine-alcohol, chlorhexidine, chlorhexidine-alcohol, or chlorhexidine-alcohol with iodine combination) did not appear to be associated with the frequency of wound surgical site infection in women undergoing unscheduled cesarean delivery with adjunctive azithromycin prophylaxis.
